checks.text: The tubers are tiny and the leaves turn brown.
The disease crushes the whole plant.
The fruit has similar patches near where they attach to the stem.
Leaves become yellow around the spots and can dry up and drop off.
The spots may join together to cover the whole leaf, causing it to turn brown.
During the rainy season plants may have dark brown rings (leaf spots), surrounded by a yellow ring.
The spots start first on the oldest leaves.
First, it causes small, water-soaked, greyish-green, irregular areas on leaves.
Later, the areas become dark grey and grow over entire leaves.
On the undersides of leaves, a fuzzy white fungal growth might be seen early in the morning or after rain.
Stem infections can girdle the plant, causing death.
Large brown leathery areas may occur on fruits.
